title: Which game engines are you all using for your games?
author: Patient-Software-168
selftext: I am currently using Godot for a sim rts game, and was wondering what everyone else uses for their AI game made projects.

comments.author: Denaton_
comments.body: None, I realized that today's AI is powerful enough to design the engine around the game instead of designing the game around the engine.

replies.author: Denaton_
replies.body: I haven't seen a difference in usage when I tried Unity, Godot and building what it needs on its own.

replies.author: eugene20
replies.body: I just struggle to believe it takes fewer tokens building your own engine first than using the hundreds of thousands/millions of lines of code from an existing one.

replies.author: Denaton_
replies.body: Because its not building an engine like Unity or Godot, it makes a very barebone minimum engine with no bloat or UI..

replies.author: eugene20
replies.body: Obviously it's not building something the same as those, they're very generalised and you're building for just your game, but it's still reinventing a ton of code.

replies.author: Denaton_
replies.body: It properly does, but it also doesn't need to find workaround to accommodate the engine so its probably why its even out.

replies.author: SmartCustard9944
replies.body:
What you might save in tokens, you end up paying in performance, limitations, etc.

Godot is a great project, but not a fan of how it is being managed. It is also a performance slog, quite consistently.

comments.author: Upbeat-Mail7201
comments.body: Godot for my main game, unity for the sideproject. Why ? I hate unity, but Godot can't do proper Voxel deformation live in multiplayer with good performance so it was not an option at all xd and Unreal is larger than my SSD 😂

comments.author: ABurningDesire
comments.body: I was using a few and then decided to make my own engine. 😄

replies.author: MKopelke
replies.body: Me too. Takes more time and effort, but you have total control over the entire project.

replies.author: ABurningDesire
replies.body: Very true. I just feel like it’s mine and not having to bend my vision to fit the engine.

replies.author: MKopelke
replies.body: Exactly. And AI means we can basically remake an entire engine in a paltry amount of time.

replies.author: amunozo1
replies.body: What advantages do you see of building your own, meaning what can you do that you could not before? How do you do it?

replies.author: MKopelke
replies.body: I just like making games in pure code and knowing that when it's playable it's because of the work I've done engineering the prompts to get the game to work the way I want it to

replies.author: zenmatrix83
replies.body: with how much better AI is getting and unity adding more restrictions and godot at least being ai neatural leaves unreal the only commercial choice which isn't good. I'm also making my own

replies.author: zenmatrix83
replies.body: 3 editor instances on one pc. It may not seem like a lot but it’s still more restrictive then before. Then they have made poor choices in the past like wanting money for every install and other things

replies.author: SmartCustard9944
replies.body:
I’m also against limitations. I just want to point out that even with a beefy PC, due to concurrent AI agents working it is constantly maxed out, which means I need to anyway start distributing my local compute across multiple computers.

Perhaps people sticking with Unity can look into remote development on multiple computers.

comments.author: jimbojohndoe
comments.body:
Godot is pretty good. So far for my 3d game it's been going pretty well, might have been easier in other engines, but it's does the job albeit quite a bit of iterations to optimize. 
For my other 2d games I don't think they had a game engine

comments.author: _HoundOfJustice
comments.body:
Unreal Engine for serious stuff and my main engine, for some hobby/fun projects im considering diving into some other engines more dedicated to pixel games which i would then get into my 3D printed and assembled hardware to toy around for fun.

I was thinking about a custom game engine too for hobby games but its very rarely worth the hustle. I have an idea here for something niche but thats a question for the future and isnt my priority.

comments.author: je386
comments.body: None, I use kotlin multiplatform  with compose multiplatform, but no game engine at all.

comments.author: TheLastNeonDev
comments.body: unity here. claude code writes basically all the c# and codex makes the 3d props. biggest thing i learned is the ai cant see the game so every fix needs a screenshot or it just guesses

comments.author: Sekhmet-CustosAurora
comments.body: Bevy. Honestly I chose it pretty arbitrarily; because I know Rust is performant and I figured a 'pure programming' engine would be better suited than something that has a lot of UI to navigate
